_comment: CPR8 / R7 BACK-COMPAT ROW: the pre-CPR8 four-hart, no-orchestrator Castalia, restored to the supported matrix as a NAMED row -- the castalia_notrapcsr precedent applied to the promotion. CPR8 made numHarts=5 + orchestrator=true the SHIPPED DEFAULT (both the _CONFIG_META entry and the _cfg call site -- the two-places rule), which by the same back door that R-DK3 opened would have removed the historical shape from the matrix entirely: no config anywhere would have set orchestrator=false, so the four-hart chip this project shipped until 2026-08-15 -- SH_AW=15, four identical hart_tile corners, hart 0 the management hart with no orch_tile wrapper, no TCM apertures, extended flash at 0x20000, PWRCR bits 1-3 -- would have become untestable without adding a file. This is that one file. It is the ONLY configuration in the tree that exercises the orchestrator=false RTL arm (MCU.vhd's non-orchestrator hart-0 emission, the SH_AW=15 memory map v1, and the aperture-less slave fabric), and it must reproduce the PRE-CPR8 golden master byte for byte. Its suite selection drops the two orchestrator rows (shorch, shtcm) and regains `shafe` (harts_le4), i.e. the 143-test list the standing suite carried before the promotion. Prove it with: SUITE=full make verify CONFIG=config/castalia4.json
_packageNote: 2026-08-16 PIN, the package sibling of the orchestrator pin above and added for the same reason. castalia-quad-qfn64 became the SHIPPED DEFAULT package model on 2026-08-16; this row does not name one, so it would have INHERITED the Castalia-Quad QFN-64 pinout AND the AFE/EIS chapter that model gates. The RTL identity this row exists to prove is UNAFFECTED by the package (the pad ring is documentation plus PnR pad-list data; MCU.vhd and MemoryMap.vhd are package-agnostic by construction and were measured byte-identical across the flip), so this pin is NOT needed for byte-identity -- it is needed for the MANUAL: at numHarts=4 / orchestrator=false the AFE figure rendered two boxes both labelled `hart 0', a gate line reading `s_master = 0 or 0', and prose promising five harts, all through a green build. The AfeSystemDiagram now ASSERTS the orchestrator shape, so this row FAILS to build without this line. myshkin-qfn44 is the model the pre-CPR8 four-hart Castalia actually carried.
_debugNote: 2026-08-17 PIN, the debug sibling of the package pin above and added for the same reason. Commit 00535af made debug.enable=true the SHIPPED DEFAULT (both the _CONFIG_META entry and the _cfg call site -- the two-places rule). This row pins a package model that bonds NO JTAG TAP, so inheriting that default makes generate.py's _checkDebugTransportBonded() a HARD ERROR: 'debug.enable is true but package model "myshkin-qfn44" bonds no JTAG TAP ... the DTM would be on-die and unreachable'. The row was unbuildable from 00535af until this line. Pinned, not changed -- debug-OFF is the shape this row already resolved to before the promotion (the DM is proven at N=5 by config/castalia_debug.json and at N=18 by config/argus_debug.json, both of which name a TAP-bearing package). The alternative fix -- moving this row to castalia-lqfp100 -- would change the chip this row exists to document.
